description: Extend rlqas-chem with four innovation directions: (1) QOP operator pool integration, (2) GRPO agent, (3) multi-objective Pareto reward, (4) experiment runners for systematic comparison. The goal is to get the best possible VQE results, not to benchmark. All changes are additive — existing rlqas-chem functionality must not be broken.

userStories.title: Implement GRPO Agent
userStories.description: As a researcher, I want a GRPO (Group Relative Policy Optimization) agent for UCC circuit search. GRPO samples G complete circuit rollouts per molecule, computes within-group relative advantages from VQE energies, and updates the policy with a clipped importance-weighted objective. No critic network is needed.
fix: config keys: lr (default 3e-4), clip_range (default 0.2), group_size G (default 4), gamma (default 0.99), entropy_coef (default 0.01)
Run one complete episode; return {states, actions, log_probs, final_energy}
Episode ends when env returns terminated=True
group_results: list of G dicts from collect_episode
energy_rewards = [r['final_energy'] for r in group_results]  (lower is better, so negate)
advantage_i = (rewards[i] - mean_r) / std_r  for each episode i
Return tensor of shape (G,) with per-episode advantage
For each episode i with advantage A_i:
For each (state, action, old_log_prob) in episode i:
Sample action from policy; return (action, log_prob)
IMPORTANT: GRPOAgent.train_one_group() drives its own episode collection internally.
The UCCSearchController must detect agent_type='grpo' and call train_one_group() per group instead of the standard step-by-step training loop.
Add grpo_search() method to UCCSearchController or handle in controller.py via agent_type check.
acceptanceCriteria: from rlqas_chem.rl import GRPOAgent
from rlqas_chem.rl import AgentFactory; assert 'grpo' in AgentFactory.supported_agents()
import rlqas_chem; r = rlqas_chem.search('H2', 0.74, ansatz_type='UCC', agent_type='grpo', n_episodes=20); assert 'best_energy' in r and r['best_energy'] < -1.0
GRPOAgent policy loss must decrease over 5 training groups on H2 (assert final_loss < initial_loss)

userStories.title: Multi-objective Pareto reward (alpha parameter)
userStories.description: As a researcher, I want to control the trade-off between energy accuracy and circuit depth via a single alpha parameter, so I can sweep alpha to generate a Pareto frontier of energy vs CNOT count.
fix: Add alpha parameter to UCCRewardFunction.__init__() with default alpha=1.0
When alpha < 1.0: energy_weight = alpha; complexity_penalty_per_op = (1.0 - alpha) * base_cnot_cost
base_cnot_cost for FOP: use 4 CNOT per operator (JW standard single/double)
base_cnot_cost for QOP: use 2 CNOT per Pauli string operator
Normalize: complexity_penalty = (1 - alpha) * (n_operators / max_operators) so it is in [0,1] range
When alpha=1.0 (default): behavior is identical to current implementation (no change)
Accept alpha in config dict (default 1.0), pass to UCCRewardFunction
Add alpha parameter to search() signature with default alpha=1.0
Pass alpha through to controller config
Add max_operators parameter to search() and controller:
If max_operators is not specified and an adapt_vqe_operators count is provided, use it
Otherwise default to existing behavior (unlimited / pool size)
acceptanceCriteria: import rlqas_chem; r = rlqas_chem.search('H2', 0.74, ansatz_type='UCC', agent_type='ppo', n_episodes=30, alpha=0.7); assert 'best_energy' in r

import rlqas_chem; r1 = rlqas_chem.search('H2', 0.74, ansatz_type='UCC', agent_type='ppo', n_episodes=30, alpha=1.0); r2 = rlqas_chem.search('H2', 0.74, ansatz_type='UCC', agent_type='ppo', n_episodes=30, alpha=0.5); assert r2.get('n_operators', 999) <= r1.get('n_operators', 999) + 5
UCCRewardFunction(alpha=1.0).compute_reward(e, n) == UCCRewardFunction().compute_reward(e, n) for any e, n (backward compatible)

userStories.title: Hyperparameter optimization with Optuna

fix: Uses Optuna TPE sampler with MedianPruner
ALL agents: lr log-uniform [1e-5, 1e-2], gamma uniform [0.9, 0.999], max_operators int [5, 20]
Pruning: report energy every 50 episodes; prune if median worse by >10%
Returns: {best_params: dict, best_energy: float, study: optuna.Study}
Add optuna as optional dependency in pyproject.toml (extras_require={'hpo': ['optuna>=3.0']})
Add CLI command: rlqas-chem optimize --molecule LiH --bond-length 1.6 --agent ppo --trials 50
